description: Each event's average remaining is compared with the mean of the per-event average remaining values, so every event carries equal weight.

b.request: For each event (`budget.link_to_event`), compute the average `spent` and average `remaining` across its budget lines (ignoring NULLs), then compute the difference between that event's average remaining and the overall mean of the per-event average remaining values (each event weighted equally), and list the top 10 events by difference descending with NULLs last, unrounded
b.sql: WITH e AS (SELECT link_to_event, AVG(spent) AS avg_spent, AVG(remaining) AS avg_remaining FROM budget GROUP BY link_to_event) SELECT link_to_event, avg_spent, avg_remaining, avg_remaining - (SELECT AVG(avg_remaining) FROM e) AS diff_from_mean_remaining FROM e ORDER BY (diff_from_mean_remaining IS NULL), diff_from_mean_remaining DESC LIMIT 10

c.request: For each event (`budget.link_to_event`), show the average `spent` and the average `remaining` across its budget lines. Also show how far its average remaining is above the overall average remaining (its average minus the overall average). Ignore missing values in the averages. List the 10 events with the largest difference, highest first, with missing values last. Don't round. Each event's average remaining is compared with the mean of the per-event average remaining values, so every event carries equal weight.
c.sql: WITH per_event AS (SELECT link_to_event, AVG(spent) AS avg_spent, AVG(remaining) AS avg_remaining FROM budget GROUP BY link_to_event) SELECT link_to_event, avg_spent, avg_remaining, avg_remaining - (SELECT AVG(avg_remaining) FROM per_event) AS diff_from_overall FROM per_event ORDER BY diff_from_overall IS NULL, diff_from_overall DESC LIMIT 10

a.request: For each event (`budget.link_to_event`), give the average `spent` and the average `remaining` across its budget lines. Also give how much its average remaining exceeds the mean of all the per-event average remaining values (each event counted once), as average remaining minus that mean. Ignore missing values in the averages. Sort by that difference, highest first, with missing values last, and show the top 10. Don't round.
a.sql: WITH per_event AS (SELECT link_to_event, AVG(spent) AS avg_spent, AVG(remaining) AS avg_remaining FROM budget GROUP BY link_to_event) SELECT link_to_event, avg_spent, avg_remaining, avg_remaining - (SELECT AVG(avg_remaining) FROM per_event) AS diff_from_mean FROM per_event ORDER BY diff_from_mean DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

d.request: For each event (`budget.link_to_event`), show the average `spent` and the average `remaining` across its budget lines, ignoring missing values. Also show how far each event's average remaining is above the overall average remaining, where the overall average is the mean of the per-event average remaining values, so every event carries equal weight. The difference is the event's average remaining minus that overall average. List the 10 events with the largest difference, highest first, with missing values last. Don't round.
d.sql: WITH per_event AS (SELECT link_to_event, AVG(spent) AS avg_spent, AVG(remaining) AS avg_remaining FROM budget WHERE link_to_event IS NOT NULL GROUP BY link_to_event) SELECT link_to_event, avg_spent, avg_remaining, avg_remaining - AVG(avg_remaining) OVER () AS diff_from_overall FROM per_event ORDER BY diff_from_overall DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10
